newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan rubber seen mixed, eyes on currency market.
newsitem.headline: Japan rubber seen mixed, eyes on currency market.

text.p: Japanese rubber futures prices are expected to be mixed this week, with market participants closely watching the volatile currency market for clues to direction, traders said on Monday.
Rubber traders are also waiting to see whether the market will be supported by the change in the Thai government's price intervention policy and moderate physical buying by Japan.
Hopes are also growing that China, which made a spate of inquiries last week, will buy in the near future.

Thailand's National Rubber Policy Committee said last week it would raise its intervention price for Ribbed Smoked Sheet (RSS3) grade rubber to 29 bahts per kg from 27.5 bahts, to help prop up the weak rubber market.
"Amid growing views that the yen will rise further (against the dollar), rubber futures prices in Japan are likely to be slightly downward biased," one analyst with a commodity brokerage house said.
He said the benchmark October rubber futures contract on the Tokyo Commodity Exchange (TOCOM) was expected to move within a range of 135 yen and 140 yen in the near term.
A weaker dollar against the yen pushes down the price of imported products to Japan.
The dollar has been rapidly weakening against the yen since the end of last week. In early Tokyo trade on Monday, the dollar slipped to a nearly four-month low of 117.50 yen.

On the change to the Thai government's intervention policy, the analyst said the move was not expected to have a large impact on rubber prices because of generally poor demand from U.S. and European consumers.
The benchmark October contract on TOCOM ended the morning session at 138.2 yen per kg, down from the Friday close of 139.6 yen.
Benchmark October on the Kobe Rubber Exchange was quoted at 137.9 yen per kg at the end of the second trading session, down from Friday's 140.2 yen close.

Although gains in the yen against the dollar would work to push Japanese rubber futures prices down, sharp losses in yen-based futures are unlikely because of steady overseas rubber prices, another analyst with a seperate commodity brokerage house said.

"As overseas markets are expected to be steady on moderate Japanese buying and potential Chinese buying, further losses in Japan's rubber futures are likely to be limited, unless the yen rises sharply above current levels," the analyst said.
Japanese traders may increase buying of physical rubber overseas because of recent strength in the yen, traders said.
Thai rubber to Japan was offered at 110 U.S. cents per kg on an FOB basis on Monday, against 108 cents on May 6.
In the local physical market, benchmark Thai rubber for large-lot end users was quoted at 151 yen on Monday, against 152 yen on May 6.
